title: Choose the visual world for Bagel's Sitter Guide
question: The roll assigned the Hawker Stall Signboard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Hawker Stall Signboard
options.thesis: The visit as a stall's menu board: numbered photo items, the exact quantity where the price goes, and a 'Now serving' number that keeps your place.
options.viewport: Yellow stall banner with a 'Now serving No. 4' display, a red door strip, the current step as a big lit tile with photo and red quantity, a thumb-zone Done button, the rest of the board below.
options.risk: Can read as a novelty if the signboard grammar spreads past type, colour and the quantity slot into the controls.

raised.raise: Every step carries the same fixed furniture: number, name, photo, one key value, one line of detail.
The one value that matters on each step (⅓ can, ½ pump, 40°C, ×2) is set at poster scale.
Hairline rules do the structuring; no boxes on boxes or decorative shadow.
Night mode is designed for a dim flat (warm, low-glare lightbox), not an inverted day theme.
Full-contrast ink only: secondary text never fades to a mid grey.

options.label: Flat-pack Assembly Booklet
options.thesis: One step per page: a huge step number, a photo, and part callouts like '⅓ ×' so the sitter follows pictures, not paragraphs.
options.viewport: A single step page: giant numeral, photo with circled callouts, a parts row of quantities, and Next to turn the page.
options.risk: The most familiar way to do step-by-step; it is where most runs for a how-to land.

options.label: Jet-age Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: The visit as a coupon book: each step is a coupon stamped USED in red, so the wallet always shows what remains.
options.viewport: A wallet header with the visit's route (door, food, litter, play, door), the current coupon on top, stamped coupons stacked behind.
options.case: Holds product clarity (stamped, never deleted) but loses audience identification: travel paperwork is less personal to a cat sitter than a hawker board.
options.risk: Formal and official in tone, which fights the owners' warm voice.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Bagel as a mascot with a fixed name plate and note under every portrait.
options.viewport: A pastel grid of rounded cells, one per step.
options.case: A ranked roster orders characters, not a timed sequence, and it sits close to the old pink look.
options.kept: Fixed per-step furniture: number, name, photo, key value.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.thesis: Giant cropped lowercase and flat colour tiles as the interface.
options.viewport: A sliding panorama of step tiles.
options.case: Cropped headlines and panorama panes hide the details sitters must read.
options.kept: Poster-scale type for the single value that matters.

options.label: Centre-rail Reference Setting
options.thesis: Twin short columns around a rail of vermilion keys.
options.viewport: Two dense text columns with a keyed centre rail.
options.case: Two dense columns of small type at arm's length on a phone.
options.kept: Hairline rules structure the page instead of boxes.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.lineage: celestial charts read by red flashlight
options.thesis: Steps plotted as stars on a navy chart.
options.viewport: A navy chart with the visit as a constellation.
options.case: A constellation does not carry a strict order or quantities.
options.kept: A night mode built for reading in the dark.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Barcode bars and monospace numerics in pure black and white.
options.case: Cold and abstract for a warm, personal guide.
options.kept: Full-contrast ink; no faded grey text.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean phone checklist app: grouped list, checkmarks, photo thumbnails, one accent colour.
canonCard.viewport: A progress header, the door warning as a banner, then a grouped list of steps with tick circles and thumbnails.
canonCard.risk: Works, but could be anyone's checklist; loses Bagel's personality.
